props.gloss_en: the mishnah: one who sees a place where miracles were done for Israel says 'Blessed... Who did miracles for our fathers in this place'
R' Yochanan: [the source is] as the verse says, 'and Jethro said: Blessed be the Lord Who delivered...' (Ex 18:10)
(the Gemara's question) over a miracle of the many we bless, and over a miracle of an individual we do not bless?!
Rava, to the man saved from a lion by the Euphrates: every time you reach there, bless 'Blessed... Who did a miracle for me in this place'

Mar son of Ravina, saved by a spring in the valley of willows and from a wild camel in Mechoza: at the willows he blessed '...Who did a miracle for me in the willows and with the camel', at Mechoza '...with the camel and in the willows'
over a miracle of the many, everyone is obligated to bless
over a miracle of an individual, he [himself] is obligated to bless

the baraita: one who sees the crossings of the sea, the crossings of the Jordan, the crossings of the streams of Arnon, the Elgavish stones on the descent of Beit Choron, the stone Og king of Bashan sought to throw on Israel, the stone Moses sat on when Joshua fought Amalek, Lot's wife, and the wall of Jericho swallowed in its place -- over all of them he must give thanks and praise before God
granted the crossings of the sea: as it is written, 'and the Israelites came into the sea on dry ground' (Ex 14:22)
the crossings of the Jordan: as it is written, 'the priests bearing the ark... stood on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan' (Josh 3:17)
but the crossings of the streams of Arnon -- from where? As it is written, 'therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: Et and Hev in Sufa...' (Num 21:14)
the tanna: 'Et and Hev in Sufa' -- they were two lepers who walked at the rear (sof) of the camp of Israel

the Emorites hid in caves in the mountains to kill Israel; when the ark came the mountains closed on one another and killed them, and their blood ran down into the streams of Arnon; Et and Hev saw the blood and told Israel, who sang
that is what is written: 'and the cascade of the streams that inclines toward the dwelling of Ar and leans upon the border of Moab' (Num 21:15)
the tanna: [Elgavish = al gav ish] stones that stood [suspended] on account of a man and came down on account of a man
stood on account of a man -- that is Moses
as it is written, 'and the man Moses was very humble' (Num 12:3)
and it is written, 'the thunder and the hail ceased, and the rain was not poured on the earth' (Ex 9:33)
came down on account of a man -- that is Joshua
as it is written, 'take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is spirit' (Num 27:18)
and it is written, 'as they fled before Israel, at the descent of Beit Choron, the Lord cast great stones on them' (Josh 10:11)
the stone Og king of Bashan sought to throw on Israel -- it is known by received tradition [not from a verse]

Og said: the camp of Israel is three parasangs; I will uproot a three-parasang mountain and throw it on them. He uprooted it and carried it on his head; the Holy One brought insects that pierced it, and it came down around his neck
he wanted to pull it off; his teeth were drawn out to this side and that, and he could not pull it off
and that is what is written, 'You broke the teeth of the wicked' (Ps 3:8)
Reish Lakish: what is 'You broke the teeth of the wicked'? Do not read shibarta (You broke) but shirbavta (You lengthened)
Moses was ten cubits tall; he took a ten-cubit axe, leapt ten cubits, struck Og on the ankle and killed him
the stone Moses sat on: as it is written, 'Moses' hands were heavy, and they took a stone and put it under him and he sat on it' (Ex 17:12)
Lot's wife: as it says, 'his wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt' (Gen 19:26)
the wall of Jericho that was swallowed: as it is written, 'and the wall fell down in its place' (Josh 6:20)
[over Lot's wife] he says 'Blessed... the true Judge'
(emend the baraita to) teach: over Lot and his wife one recites two blessings
and over Lot he says 'Blessed... Who remembers the righteous'
R' Yochanan: even in the hour of His anger the Holy One remembers the righteous
as it says, 'when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of the overthrow' (Gen 19:29)
